title: Split parquet leaks if the bare `os.unlink(data_path)` at line 821 raises after the split file was written
description: `_split_data` writes the split parquet to `split_path` (lines 789-807) and then, on success, removes the prepared input with a bare `os.unlink(data_path)` (line 821) — bypassing the loud-but-safe `_remove_temp_parquet` helper used everywhere else in this module. If that `os.unlink` raises an `OSError` (e.g. a transient Windows file lock, EBUSY, or a permission/network-FS hiccup on the temp dir), the exception propagates out of `_split_data` BEFORE it can `return _SplitResult(...)`. Because `_SplitResult` was never returned, `run()`'s `split_result` stays `None`, so the `finally` -> `_cleanup_owned_temp_parquets(prepared, split_result)` only considers `prepared` and never sees `split_path`. The freshly written split parquet (potentially multi-GB) is therefore orphaned in the OS temp dir — exactly the failure mode the remediation-4b.6 cleanup net (run() lines 550-558) was built to prevent. The same bare-unlink pattern at `_prepare_data` line 707 has the analogous shape, though there `data_path` is still tracked by `prepared` so the leak is narrower. The dedicated cleanup test suite (tests/test_training_temp_cleanup.py) exercises cancellation and metrics/validation failures but has no case where the inline `os.unlink` itself fails, so this window is untested.
evidence: _split_data: split_path created (789-794) and written via bounded_sink (803); on the failure branch only split_path is removed (812-814); on success line 821 does `os.unlink(data_path)` then line 824 `return _SplitResult(... owns_tmp=True)`. If line 821 throws, the function raises pre-return, so run() (474-478) gets no split_result; the finally at 558 calls _cleanup_owned_temp_parquets(prepared, None) which builds candidates only from prepared (573-576) — split_path is never a candidate and leaks. Every other temp deletion in the module routes through _remove_temp_parquet (which swallows OSError to a warning), but lines 707 and 821 use a raw os.unlink.
